done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. `TEST_NAME` stops a pytest node ID at a comma or semicolon. A worker can name a valid parameter case such as `tests/test_login.py::test_role[staff,active]`; Close extracts only `tests/test_login.py::test_role[staff`, cannot match it to the case that ran, and publishes `not run` instead of its result. The command test covers parameter IDs without punctuation.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate. The worker guidance allows every Done-when detail next to its test, but this line keeps only the text before the first test name. For a line such as `- Greeting: tests/test_greeting.py::test_returning (including empty names)`, Close removes the parenthesized detail from both the pull request and review proof list. The reviewer can then approve a list that omits a required detail.
findings.title: Not done: proof list drops Done-when details written after a test name

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 1-2, reversible; third finding in review.py, so one general rule instead of per-language cases): any proof line naming a test that close cannot match to its own run's results, in any language, is published as not checked; reading JavaScript runners' per-test results is a follow-up. The failed-test case gets its assertion this round.

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
